h1: Hotel De Nara — a Lanna boutique inside the old city walls, within walking distance of everything
intro: Picture this: a dark-brown teak hotel dressed up with woven textiles and Lanna home décor, tucked into a small lane inside the old city walls, just a few minutes' walk from Chiang Mai Gate, the Chiang Mai Gate market, the old temples and the Sunday Walking Street — Hotel De Nara is a small boutique hotel that a lot of people pick because it gives you a genuine Lanna-Thai feel, a downtown location, and a little saltwater pool to soak in, all at a price that's still within reach · 23 rooms, from around THB 1,100/night

body.html: Hotel De Nara positions itself as a small Lanna-style boutique hotel on Moon Muang Road Lane 2 in the Phra Sing area, inside Chiang Mai's old city walls · What gets it talked about among travelers is its location, which puts you within walking distance of almost everything in the old city — Chiang Mai Gate and the Chiang Mai Gate market about 5 min away, Tha Phae Gate about 7 min, and Wat Phra Singh, Wat Chedi Luang and the Sunday Walking Street all an easy stroll · The hotel itself is a multi-story building arranged around the pool, decorated with teak, woven fabrics and local home furnishings, and once you step off the main road into the lane, the atmosphere is quieter and shadier than you'd expect — plenty of reviewers call it a little oasis in the middle of the old city · What makes Hotel De Nara interesting isn't that it's big or fancy, but that it hits exactly what most people coming to Chiang Mai want: a stay in a genuine Lanna-Thai setting, in a spot where you can step out and start exploring on foot without doing the math on taxi fares, and on a budget that won't blow out · This review is put together from the voices of people who have actually stayed, drawn from the main booking platforms and public reviews; we're not claiming the team stayed here ourselves, so you can see both the praise and the genuine criticism before you hit book

As for who this hotel suits, the real reviews answer that pretty clearly · It's a great fit for couples, solo travelers and the temple-and-walking-street crowd who want to stay in the heart of the old city without paying luxury-hotel prices · With just 23 rooms, the vibe is friendly and quiet, none of the bustle of a big hotel · On the flip side, if you're coming as a large family that needs several connecting rooms, a big pool, or full resort-style facilities, this may not be your first pick, because the main draw here is boutique charm and location rather than size and luxury · The group that consistently leaves clearly positive reviews is couples on a honeymoon or a weekend getaway, plus international travelers who come specifically to soak up old-city life — temple-hopping, taking photos, sampling local food · The people who may not click with it are business travelers who want meeting rooms and a full gym, or anyone who's a really light sleeper and wants the dead silence of a suburban resort · Knowing which group you're in before you book helps the experience match your expectations so you don't end up disappointed later

Location and getting around is Hotel De Nara's single biggest strength · The hotel sits in the southwestern corner of the old city walls, near Chiang Mai Gate, which is the starting point of Wua Lai Road and the evening food market · The Sunday Walking Street (Ratchadamnoen Road) and the Saturday Walking Street (Wua Lai Road) are both within walking distance, so on weekends you barely need to call a car at all · From Chiang Mai Airport (CNX) it's about 4 km, roughly a 15–20 min drive · If you'd rather not walk all day, grabbing a Grab or a red songthaew from the front of the hotel is easy, and staff can help arrange it · The upside of being inside the old city walls is that most of the inner lanes make for easy walking, shaded by trees and old buildings, so you can wander from temple to temple at a relaxed pace without worrying too much about traffic · Historic temples like Wat Chedi Luang and Wat Phra Singh, plus the small temples tucked away in the lanes, are good for almost a full day of strolling · If you want to head out to the Nimmanhaemin area for modern cafés and restaurants, that's about a 12–15 min drive, while getting up to Doi Suthep or over to Warorot Market (Kad Luang) is also easy from this central spot, with cars simple to flag down

All 23 rooms are done up in a Lanna-Thai theme — wooden beds, local woven textiles, warm brown tones — with Superior, Deluxe King/Queen, Large Twin, and rooms with a spa bath in some categories · Rooms come with air-conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a fridge, an electric kettle, a work desk and free Wi-Fi · Bathrooms have a water heater and all the basic amenities · Many reviews praise the rooms as clean, charmingly decorated and good value given the downtown location · But some voices say plainly that the beds are on the firm side for some people, and certain room types are compact — better suited to travelers without much luggage · What a lot of people single out as a plus is the decorative detail: the carved wooden headboards, fabric lamps and local-style touches that make you feel like you're really staying in Chiang Mai, not just any generic hotel room · The rooms with their own spa bath are a favorite for couples to book because they offer a private, relaxing atmosphere · The tip from reviews is that if you're traveling as a pair with big suitcases, choose a Deluxe-level room or above so you have space for your luggage and room to move comfortably, while solo travelers or those keeping it budget will find a Superior room enough for a night's rest after a full day out
"Small but lovely hotel, beautifully decorated in Lanna style. A few minutes' walk out of the lane gets you to Chiang Mai Gate and the Walking Street, and the staff were helpful with everything."

At the heart of the hotel is the outdoor saltwater pool that many people love, because the mild salt water doesn't sting your eyes like heavy chlorine, making it perfect for a cooling soak after a full day out · Around the pool there are sun loungers and quiet little spots to sit · There's also an in-house spa and Thai massage service, which is handy for anyone who's walked themselves tired and doesn't want to go out hunting for a massage shop · There's a 24-hour front desk, laundry service and free on-site parking · To be honest, the pool isn't large and is better for a relaxing soak than for swimming laps; anyone hoping for a long resort-style pool may find it a touch small · To make the most of the pool, reviews suggest the early morning and the late-afternoon soft light are the nicest times — fewer people, quiet, and Chiang Mai's air just about perfect · As for the spa, the in-house Thai massage is a good match for the all-day walker, because you just book at the front desk and walk over with no time wasted heading out; it isn't a big spa with a huge menu of treatments like a resort, but it's plenty for easing the aches after a day on your feet

On food and drink, the hotel has its own restaurant serving Thai dishes and breakfast · Breakfast is one of the things reviews speak well of — there are both Thai and international options, some items cooked fresh to order, and you can eat in a quiet garden setting · For other meals, the location here is a real advantage, because a few minutes' walk gets you to the Chiang Mai Gate market, packed with local food in the evening — khao soi, khanom jeen nam ngiao and budget-friendly street food · And anyone who likes a morning coffee has plenty of old-city cafés to choose from and stroll to

Service is another point reviews praise in agreement again and again · Many staff get mentioned as friendly, easygoing, and good at helping with tour bookings, calling cars and recommending restaurants in the area · Thanks to the small size, the staff remember guests and look after them fairly attentively — a charm that many big hotels can't offer · The overall feel is a small hotel that leans into warmth and privacy, well suited to anyone who wants a clean, charming, well-located place to stay and then spends most of their time out exploring the old city · There are quite a few reviews from people who came back to stay again on a later trip, which is a good sign that the overall experience matched expectations with nothing major to disappoint

If you try to distill the real reviews into a clearer picture, the praise that comes up most often is the walk-everywhere location, the charming Lanna-style decor, the cleanliness of the rooms, and how helpful the staff are · Many people say they were surprised to get this much boutique atmosphere at a mid-range price · On the criticism side, what shows up most is late-night noise on some nights, beds that are too firm for some people, and the compact size of the rooms/pool · A few reviews mention booking confirmation or miscommunication issues at times, which is something you can head off by confirming with the hotel again before you travel · The overall picture is a hotel that does well what it set out to be, with most of the gripes being predictable for a small hotel in the middle of a tourist area

"Clean room, nicely decorated, great location, easy walk to the Walking Street and the Chiang Mai Gate market. But on Saturday night there was some music from the bars nearby — light sleepers should ask for an inner room."

Comparing the value against hotels in the same area · Chiang Mai's old city has a lot of boutique hotels and guesthouses in the THB 1,000–3,000 range · Where Hotel De Nara has the edge is that it has a saltwater pool and an in-house spa, which most similarly priced guesthouses don't · Compared with De Lanna Hotel, which is in the same area and has more rooms, Hotel De Nara feels more private and quieter thanks to fewer rooms, though that trade-off comes with fewer facilities · Compared with upper-tier hotels like Tamarind Village or 137 Pillars House, the price is several times apart, so De Nara is the choice for anyone who wants Lanna charm and a good location without paying luxury rates · In short, it's good value within its own price bracket, as long as your expectations match what a small hotel can deliver

Things worth knowing before you book, gathered from real reviews · One, noise — if you're a light sleeper, note it when booking or call to ask for a room deeper inside on a quieter floor, and pack earplugs for the weekend nights · Two, booking confirmation — it's worth emailing or messaging the hotel to confirm again before you travel, especially if you booked through a platform during high season · Three, rooms — if you're two people with big bags or want a spa bath, choose a Deluxe-level or Spa Bath room from the start · Four, breakfast — check at booking whether breakfast is included, because some rates don't include it · Five, getting around — if you come during Yi Peng/Loy Krathong or Songkran, the roads around the old city close in places, so plan ahead for cars and luggage

The thing to say straight from real reviews is nighttime noise at certain times · Because the hotel is in an old-city area with bars and nightlife scattered around, some reviews note hearing music or sounds from nearby venues late on some nights, especially on weekends · There are also remarks about beds being on the firm side, a small pool, and certain room types being compact · Anyone who's a light sleeper or sensitive to noise should ask for a room deeper inside or on a quieter floor when booking, and have earplugs ready for Friday-Saturday nights just in case

On price and value · Hotel De Nara starts at around THB 1,100–1,400/night for a standard room in the normal season, rising to THB 1,800–2,500 for larger rooms or during high season · Compared with other boutique hotels right in the old city, this price counts as good value, especially when you get the saltwater pool, in-house spa and a location within walking distance of the Walking Street · The overall score from real reviews sits around 8.2–8.4 on the main platforms and 4.0/5 on TripAdvisor, which reflects that most people are happy with the location, cleanliness and service, while most of the gripes are about noise and the size of the rooms/pool

The bottom line from real reviews: Hotel De Nara suits travelers who want to stay in the heart of the old city, walk to the temples and the Walking Street, in a Lanna boutique setting at a price within reach · If you plan to spend most of your time outside the hotel, value location and charm over size and a full set of facilities, and aren't fussed about late-night noise in a tourist area — this place delivers that well at a reasonable price · But if you want a spacious room, a big pool, dead silence, or resort-level facilities, you might look at a higher-tier hotel along the Ping River or in the suburbs · Overall, Hotel De Nara is a good example of a small boutique hotel that knows what it's good at — location, Lanna charm, and friendly service — and does that well at a price most people can afford · If you book with expectations that match what the hotel is, while leaving a little room for the noise and room size, there's a good chance you'll come away as one more positive review

honestSummary: Hotel De Nara is the best boutique hotel for anyone who wants a heart-of-the-old-city location, the ability to walk to the temples and the Walking Street, plus Lanna charm and a saltwater pool, at a price within reach · But you have to accept that there's late-night noise on some nights, beds are on the firm side, and the pool/some room types are small
honestChecks: If you're a light sleeper sensitive to noise — the hotel is in a tourist area with bars, with late-night noise on some nights especially weekends → ask for a room deeper inside or on a quieter floor, and have earplugs ready

If you want a big pool or spacious resort-style rooms — the pool is the relaxing-soak kind and some room types are compact → choose a Deluxe-level room or above, or look at a Ping River resort if space is the priority
If it's high season (Nov–Feb) or the Yi Peng festival and you haven't booked yet — the hotel has only 23 rooms and fills up fast → book 1–2 months ahead and pick free cancellation to be safe

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Hotel De Nara Chiang Mai

faq.q: Where is Hotel De Nara · what's nearby?
faq.a: Hotel De Nara is located at 33 Moon Muang Road Lane 2, Phra Sing, Mueang Chiang Mai, inside the old city walls · It's about a 5 min walk to Chiang Mai Gate and the Chiang Mai Gate market, 7 min to Tha Phae Gate, 10 min to Wat Phra Singh, and the Sunday Walking Street is within walking distance · It's about a 12 min drive from the Night Bazaar and around 15–20 min by car from Chiang Mai Airport

faq.q: What's the starting price at Hotel De Nara · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 1,100/night for a Superior room · Larger rooms include Deluxe King/Queen and rooms with a spa bath in some categories, at around THB 1,500–2,000 · All are decorated in Lanna style with air-conditioning, a TV, a fridge and free Wi-Fi · High-season prices go up, so it's worth comparing several platforms before booking

faq.q: Who is Hotel De Nara good for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, solo travelers and anyone who wants to stay in the heart of the old city, walk to the temples and the Walking Street, in a Lanna boutique setting at a price within reach · It's a small 23-room hotel, friendly and quiet · It isn't the first pick for large families wanting connecting rooms, a big pool, or full resort-style facilities

faq.q: Does Hotel De Nara have a pool and a spa?
faq.a: Yes · an outdoor saltwater pool that doesn't sting the eyes, perfect for a cooling soak after a day out · There's an in-house spa and Thai massage service, handy for anyone who's walked themselves tired · The pool isn't large, better for a relaxing soak than for swimming laps

faq.q: What downsides should you know about Hotel De Nara before booking?
faq.a: The most common gripes from reviews are late-night noise on some nights from the bars/venues in the tourist area, beds on the firm side, and certain room types/the pool being compact · If you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, ask for a room deeper inside or on a quieter floor when booking, and have earplugs ready for Friday-Saturday nights

faq.q: How far ahead should you book?
faq.a: During high season (November–February) and the Yi Peng/Loy Krathong festival, rooms fill up very fast because there are only 23 of them, so book 1–2 months ahead · At other times, 2–3 weeks ahead is enough · Every platform has a Free Cancellation option — pick that to be safe if your plans aren't set
